name: An Off-Cycle Passive Shore Costs Its Order Plus One
statement: For a directed holonomy cycle of length $k$, put $\varepsilon=|K|-|L|-3k$. Every nonempty passive shore satisfies $|S_z|\le\varepsilon+2$ when it is a cycle shore and $|S_z|\le\varepsilon-1$ otherwise. Equivalently, a cycle shore costs at least $|S_z|-2$ units of excess, while a shore outside the cycle costs at least $|S_z|+1$.
proof: A cycle shore contributes its explicit $|S_i|-2$ summand to the holonomy excess decomposition. An off-cycle shore uses an additional passive coordinate, contributing at least one to $|Z_0|-k$. Every concept it contains has one more passive incidence than its cycle incidence, so its exponential incidence term contributes at least one more. These $|S_z|+1$ nonnegative charges give the second bound.
